target_claim: Running Dijkstra's min-key algorithm with reinsertions on the explicitly constructed DAG Gn from source a0 performs at least 2^n invocations of RELAX.
source_quote:
For every n ≥1 there is a weighted DAG Gn (with vertices a0, b1, a1, . . . , bn, an, t, hence
|V (Gn)| = 2n + 2) such that running Dijkstra’s min-key algorithm (with reinsertions on
decreases) on Gn from source a0 performs at least 2n invocations of RELAX.
test_sketch: Implement the fully specified Gn (B=4n+5, W_i=B^(n-i); edges a_{i-1}->a_i w=0, a_{i-1}->b_i w=W_i, b_i->a_i w=-W_i-1, a_n->t w=0) and Dijkstra with a min-heap that re-inserts on any key decrease, counting RELAX invocations (edges scanned per extraction). Instrumented counts for n=1..12 give relax = 5,12,22,35,51,70,92,117,145,176,210,247 (~3n^2/2 growth); at n=7 the count is 92 < 2^7 = 128, refuting the claimed >=2^n lower bound, with the gap widening for all larger n. Root cause: each indirect shortcut lowers a distance by exactly 1 and the solution itself proves -d[a_j] <= n, so each a_j is extracted at most n+1 times and the doubling recurrence T_i >= 2T_{i-1} is false.
